complexity.notes: s.lower() allocates an O(n) copy; space could be O(1) by lowercasing per-character (e.g. s[a].lower()) instead. The inner b-decrement loop needs no explicit bounds check because it is guaranteed to stop at s[a], which is alphanumeric. With the printable-ASCII character set, str.isalnum() coincides exactly with [A-Za-z0-9], so no Unicode-alnum pitfall arises here.
complexity.summary: Two-pointer scan from both ends, skipping non-alphanumeric characters and comparing lowercased characters until the pointers meet. Each pointer moves monotonically inward, so the total work is linear.
